items.claim: Both seams of this row carry byte-tier evidence and its mark handling is complete, but the rejected alternative's load-bearing form label — an asyndetic catalogue — is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which show a waw-coordinated series.
items.evidence: Confirmed: the opening run כִּ֣י י֞וֹם is verse-initial at byte tier, and the closing refrain clause is verse-final and byte-identical to the earlier site (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier). No parashah mark falls inside this span; the mark cited sits at the verse immediately before the row and is correctly typed SETUMAH, so mark handling is complete and honest. The defect is a byte-checkable form claim. Every member of the catalogue opens with the same conjunction-plus-preposition token — וְעַל֙ at the first member and וְעַ֖ל at the last, with the two between them carrying that token as well — so the series is waw-coordinated, that is polysyndetic, the opposite of asyndetic; the governing verse itself coordinates its second phrase the same way. The mislabel is repeated in the device note, and the accompanying description calls the quantifier a preposition, which it is not. Corrected, the warrant survives: a waw-coordinated series still hangs on the governing temporal clause and is still enumeration inside its oracle, so the bounds are not defeated — but the form label as written is false to the bytes, and form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits. Secondarily, the flight-from-terror device (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) brackets this row entirely with no member inside its span, straddling both of its seams, and is undisclosed here too.

items.evidence: Confirmed: the opening run כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is verse-initial at byte tier; the closing SETUMAH is correctly typed and is the only parashah mark inside the span (1 marked verse of 209 book-wide); the PETUCHAH cited at the opening seam is correctly typed; neither of the chapter's two ketiv/qere verses falls inside this span, so nothing is owed there. The woe-lexeme distinction is byte-true and matches the staged census: the interjection stands at א֣וֹי and א֖וֹי in this span — the interjection is a 4-verse object, while a bare three-letter consonantal sweep returns 8 verses, the other 4 being contained-consonant hits inside unrelated words for enemy, desire and fool — and it is a different lexeme from ה֣וֹי (sweep: 22 verses, skeleton tier). But the row states all of this in transliteration only, with no pointed splice for either lexeme: insufficient engagement on a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim in a book where that pair is a named blending hazard. The substantive gap: the span's tenth verse opens with אִמְר֥וּ, a 2mp imperative (byte tier at this site; the same pointed form stands at accent-stripped tier in 5 verses book-wide, every one an imperative address). The row's rejected alternative rules out an earlier cut precisely because that verse carries no fresh imperative, vocative or divine-speech formula of its own; by the row's own criterion the imperative two verses later is a live in-span rival, and it is neither disclosed nor disposed. The default-larger-unit rule can still absorb it, so the span is not defeated — the rival disposal is incomplete.

items.claim: The row's opening seam signal is not discriminating on the bytes — the identical temporal formula sits mid-verse in the verse immediately before it — and the supporting echo claim mis-states both the attached form and the matching tier while bracketing a work partition rather than a unit of text.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: the opening run is verse-initial at byte tier; the PETUCHAH at the closing verse and the SETUMAH at the opening seam are correctly typed and are the only parashah marks in and at the span (2 marked verses of 209 book-wide); the remnant participle הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר re-collates at byte tier and does belong to the reactivating verb family in the staged census; and the referent of the branch is properly left undecided. First defect: the verse immediately before this row carries בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ mid-verse against בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא verse-initial here — the two agree at accent-stripped and at skeleton tier and differ only in accentuation, so the formula straddles the row's own opening seam undisclosed. The formula is dense in this stretch: 7 verses across chapters 2-4 (skeleton tier — oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.17, oshb:Isa.2.20, oshb:Isa.3.7, oshb:Isa.3.18, oshb:Isa.4.1, oshb:Isa.4.2; sweep: 45 verses book-wide), and it is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.18 as well, where it is read as enumeration inside a unit rather than as a seam. The same recurrence class is disclosed for oshb:Isa.2.20 elsewhere in this cluster, so the omission here is an unexplained asymmetry, not an oversight of class. Second defect: the echo claim is false to the bytes on both counts. The earlier site reads כְּסֻכָּ֣ה with an attached preposition and this row's site reads וְסֻכָּ֛ה with an attached conjunction, not a preposition; and as tokens their consonantal skeletons differ, so they do not match at skeleton tier at all, while the unprefixed noun matches at accent-stripped tier — one tier above the claim. The noun itself stands at exactly 2 verses once the molten-image homograph is excluded (sweep: 6 verses, skeleton tier, of which 4 are the homograph at oshb:Isa.25.7, oshb:Isa.28.20, oshb:Isa.30.1, oshb:Isa.42.17). Third: that echo is asserted as bracketing a work partition's own opening and closing images, and the closing mark is placed at the close of a work partition's assigned range — a bracket claimed over a workflow unit rather than over any unit of the text, in row prose. Finally, a smaller blend: the row's second remnant word וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ (sweep: 1 verse) is from a different root than the family its signal key names, and that same root also opens the earlier echo verse as וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה — a live link the row does not mention while disclosing the weaker one.
